Family paid tribute to Bristol University geology student, 18, after being notified by Avon and Somerset police A body has been found in the search for an 18-year-old British man who went missing last year while hiking in Romania, UK police said. George Smyth, a geology student at the University of Bristol, went missing in November. On Saturday, Avon and Somerset police said a body found in the Bucegi Mountain region of the country is believed to be that of Smyth. His family have been informed and are being supported by a family liaison officer, the force added. Smyth’s family said: “We are all devastated by George’s death. “He was the best of us and is deeply missed by his younger brothers, family and friends.

A body has been found in the search for a missing British teenager who went missing while hiking in Romania. George Smyth, a geology university student from Bristol, went missing in November last year trying to hike to Bran, the village known for its castle suggested to be the home of Dracula. Avon and Somerset Police said a body has been found in the Bucegi Mountain region of the country, which is believed to be that of Mr Smyth, although formal identification has yet to take place. Officers have informed Mr Smyth’s family of the development and are being supported by a family liaison officer. They shared a statement expressing gratitude to those who have supported the search for Mr Smyth and asked for privacy and time to grieve and process what has happened.

Tributes are being paid to an 18-year-old who went missing on a hiking trip to the Romanian mountains. George Smyth, a University of Bristol student from Shropshire, had been missing since 23 November in the Bucegi mountains, despite daily searches, Brașov Mountain Rescue said. Avon and Somerset Police confirmed they had been notified by Romanian local authorities that a body had been found in the region. While formal identification has not yet taken place, the body is believed to be his. "We are all devastated by George's death. He was the best of us and is deeply missed by his younger brothers, family and friends," his family said.

[Lähde: The Guardian World | URL: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/15/body-found-in-romania-believed-to-be-missing-british-hiker-george-smyth]
Family paid tribute to Bristol University geology student, 18, after being notified by Avon and Somerset police

A body has been found in the search for an 18-year-old British man who went missing last year while hiking in Romania, UK police said.

George Smyth, a geology student at the University of Bristol, went missing in November.

On Saturday, Avon and Somerset police said a body found in the Bucegi Mountain region of the country is believed to be that of Smyth.

His family have been informed and are being supported by a family liaison officer, the force added.

Smyth’s family said: “We are all devastated by George’s death.

“He was the best of us and is deeply missed by his younger brothers, family and friends.

“We want to thank Salvamont mountain rescue, who have worked tirelessly since November searching for George, despite very difficult and often dangerous conditions.

“They are an amazing team, and have remained in constant communication, helping us greatly throughout this awful time.”

Efforts will be made to return Smyth’s body to the UK once formal identification has taken place.

The family’s statement added: “We would also like to thank Avon and Somerset police and University of Bristol, who have gone above and beyond to try and find George, and to support us as a family.

“Although this latest news is incredibly painful, the torture of waiting is finally over, so we can now focus on bringing George home and saying goodbye.

“We would appreciate privacy while we continue to come to terms with this loss.”

On Wednesday, mountain rescue teams said they had resumed their search in “previously indicated areas, under rock walls, in grates and in the hard-to-reach sectors” but without success.

The student, from Newport in Shropshire, is believed to have left Poiana Brașov heading to Bran. He reached Țigănești, where he made an emergency call for help.

At the time, rescuers said he was in a “very isolated and hard to access mountain area” and the weather conditions were extremely severe with strong winds, heavy snowfall and dense fog.

The search and rescue operation also involved a canine unit, drones and helicopters being deployed.

Sebastian Marinescu, from the area’s mountain rescue service, previously told the BBC the 18-year-old “was disoriented, physically exhausted, and already showing signs of hypothermia” when they received the emergency call.

Tributes are being paid to an 18-year-old who went missing on a hiking trip to the Romanian mountains.

George Smyth, a University of Bristol student from Shropshire, had been missing since 23 November in the Bucegi mountains, despite daily searches, Brașov Mountain Rescue said.

Avon and Somerset Police confirmed they had been notified by Romanian local authorities that a body had been found in the region. While formal identification has not yet taken place, the body is believed to be his.

"We are all devastated by George's death. He was the best of us and is deeply missed by his younger brothers, family and friends," his family said.

They added: "We want to thank Salvamont Mountain Rescue, who have worked tirelessly since November searching for George; despite very difficult and often dangerous conditions. They are an amazing team, and have remained in constant communication, helping us greatly throughout this awful time.

"We would also like to thank Avon and Somerset Police and University of Bristol, who have gone above and beyond to try and find George, and to support us as a family.

"Although this latest news is incredibly painful, the torture of waiting is finally over, so we can now focus on bringing George home and saying goodbye. We would appreciate privacy while we continue to come to terms with this loss."

Prior to going missing Smyth had contacted rescuers from Tiganesti to say he was disoriented and physically exhausted.

At the time, rescuers said he was in a "very isolated and hard-to-access mountain area" and the weather conditions were extremely severe with strong winds, heavy snowfall, and dense fog.

After news of his disappearance first broke, Smyth's former school, Haberdashers' Adams in Newport, said: "We are deeply concerned and saddened to learn that our much-loved and cherished former student, George Smyth, has been reported missing while hiking in the Bucegi Mountain Range in Romania."

Smyth's rugby club, Newport (Salop) RUFC, had been following the search effort for him and posting verified updates when possible.

They previously spoke about how Smyth was a valued member of the group.

"George is a much-loved member of our club", they said. "He grew up through our junior section, represented our Colts last season, and has often given his time wholeheartedly to help coach our younger age groups."
